title: Enterprise Compliance and Data Residency Layer
summary: Enforce tenant-approved data classification, location, lifecycle, access, transfer, retention and deletion controls with evidence-backed policy decisions.

intent.statement: Govern data as a policy-enforced lifecycle so tenant data is handled only through approved purpose, classification, location, retention and processor paths.
desired_outcomes: Every in-scope asset and flow has classification, owner, purpose, profile and lifecycle policy.
Unknown or unapproved data destinations/processors are denied.
Compliance evidence is scope-qualified and does not overstate legal/certification status.

success_measures.name: Inventory coverage
success_measures.target: 100% in-scope production data classes/flows have approved inventory and residency profile
success_measures.measurement_method: Reconcile data-flow registry with production stores/processors.

success_measures.name: Denied unapproved egress
success_measures.target: 0 unapproved restricted/confidential external processing paths succeed
success_measures.measurement_method: Policy enforcement and negative integration suite.

problem.statement: Storage-location flags alone cannot govern copies, backups, telemetry, model providers, tools, support access, recovery and data lifecycle, exposing enterprise data to unapproved processing or unsupported compliance claims.
problem.current_state: Platform has security, Vault, HA/DR and telemetry controls but lacks a unified data inventory/residency/lifecycle/processor policy layer.
impact: Data may reach unapproved destinations or processors.
Evidence may overstate legal or residency assurance.

evidence.label: High Availability and Disaster Recovery Layer

business_context.business_value: A verifiable data-control plane enables enterprise policy requirements without asserting unsupported legal compliance.

stakeholders.name: Data Governance and Compliance
stakeholders.role: Owns policy profile and evidence scope

stakeholders.name: Security Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns enforcement and sensitive data controls

actors.name: Tenant Administrator
goals: Manage approved data governance profile under policy.

actors.name: Compliance Policy Enforcement Point
goals: Allow deny or gate data operations.

actors.name: Registered Processor
goals: Process approved data only for approved purpose/location.

functional_requirements.title: Maintain data inventory
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall maintain a versioned inventory of data assets and flows with classification, owner, tenant/project scope, purpose, storage/processing locations, processors, retention and deletion metadata.

provenance.rationale: Data lifecycle must be visible to policy.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce residency profiles
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall define tenant-approved residency profiles and enforce them before data create/read/process/replicate/backup/restore/export/support/provider operations.

provenance.rationale: Residency covers all data copies/processing paths.

functional_requirements.title: Govern processors and egress
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall maintain approved processor and egress registry entries with location, purpose, data class, control status and policy constraints.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce data lifecycle
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall enforce versioned retention, archival, hold, deletion and backup-aging policies with truthful lifecycle evidence.

provenance.rationale: Retention and deletion need governed lifecycle.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce compliance decisions across boundaries
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall enforce classification/residency-aware data access, support, telemetry, extension, API, model-provider and export decisions and require authorised time-bound exceptions for otherwise disallowed operations.

provenance.rationale: All data boundaries enforce same policy.

functional_requirements.title: Preserve recovery and reporting governance
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall preserve residency/classification during recovery and produce scope-qualified control/data-flow/exception evidence without unsupported certification claims.

provenance.rationale: Recovery and reports cannot escape data governance.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Unknown/unregistered location, processor, purpose, classification or transfer destination shall deny affected data operation or require explicit approved exception.
Deletion and recovery evidence shall distinguish completed primary/replica action from residual backup-aging or restoration constraints and must not overclaim completion.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: End-to-end deletion/hold/recovery lifecycle tests inspect evidence state.
non_functional_requirements.target: Every deletion/recovery event reports truthful residual status.

business_rules.statement: A data operation requires resolved asset/classification, tenant/project, purpose, source/destination location, processor/profile and retention/hold state; missing fact denies safely.
Restricted data, secret material and private reasoning cannot be sent to unapproved processors or raw telemetry; approved exception is narrow time/purpose/location bound and evidenced.
A legal/contractual hold blocks routine deletion until an authorised release; evidence preserves hold/deletion state and residual backup aging.

constraints.statement: This specification is not legal advice or certification and authorises no legal/regulatory claim, processor onboarding, external transfer, customer residency promise or production lifecycle setting.
constraints.rationale: Qualified legal, privacy, security, customer and architecture approval is required.

dependencies.name: Residency-aware storage processing and processor topology
dependencies.risk: Supported locations/processors/backup paths require architecture and contractual decisions.

bounded_contexts.name: Data Governance and Compliance
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own data inventory/classification/residency/lifecycle/processor/exception controls and scope-qualified evidence.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Registered data class/record/flow governed by classification/purpose/lifecycle controls.
Registered internal or external destination that processes data for approved purpose/location.

workflows.name: Evaluate governed data operation
workflows.trigger: System or user requests data processing transfer export backup restore or deletion.

steps.action: Resolves asset classification, tenant/project, purpose, residency profile, processor/destination and lifecycle state.

steps.result: Operation is allowed, denied or time-bound exception gated.
Decision scope and residual status are reconstructable.

outcomes: Data is handled only through policy-approved lifecycle.
workflows.error_handling: Unknown location/processor/purpose denies; hold conflict blocks deletion.

states.name: DELETED
states.description: Primary/replica action completed; residual backup state recorded.

security_requirements.statement: Every in-scope data boundary shall enforce tenant/profile/classification/purpose/location/processor/lifecycle policy before access, egress, processing, backup or recovery.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security tests cover unknown destination, cross-profile transfer, restricted provider use, hold conflict and recovery reactivation.

observability_requirements.statement: Data operation, transfer, exception, hold, deletion, recovery and report lifecycle shall emit safe correlated Ledger evidence.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Reconstruct governed operation and residual lifecycle state from evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Data operation requires complete profile facts
acceptance_criteria.then: Classification purpose tenant and approved residency/processor facts are required or denied.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unapproved destination is blocked
acceptance_criteria.given: Backup telemetry or provider dispatch targets unapproved destination.
acceptance_criteria.then: Operation is denied or requires exception before leaving boundary.

acceptance_criteria.title: Exception is narrow and evidenced
acceptance_criteria.then: It is purpose/time/location bound with Ledger evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Hold blocks routine deletion
acceptance_criteria.then: Hold blocks deletion and release needs authorised workflow.

acceptance_criteria.title: Deletion evidence is truthful
acceptance_criteria.then: Evidence distinguishes primary replica validation and backup-aging/residual state.

acceptance_criteria.title: Recovery preserves profile
acceptance_criteria.then: Data remains in approved profile and reactivation requires policy checks.

acceptance_criteria.title: Report avoids unsupported claim
acceptance_criteria.then: Scope version evidence and exceptions are shown without unsupported certification claim.

test_requirements.scope: Processor egress unknown-destination and exception policy.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Blocked transfer and scoped exception evidence.

risks.title: Unsupported residency or lifecycle claim causes data/governance failure
risks.description: A missing flow, processor or backup path can violate policy or create unsupported compliance representation.
risks.mitigation: Inventory/egress enforcement, deny unknown, exception governance, recovery controls and scope-qualified evidence.

open_questions.question: Which tenant residency profiles locations transfers and processor conditions are supportable?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Production residency policy cannot be configured.

open_questions.question: What retention deletion hold and backup-aging schedules apply by data class and contract?

architecture_decisions.title: Use inventory-backed residency and lifecycle policy at every data boundary
architecture_decisions.context: Enterprise data may move through databases, backups, telemetry, providers, tools and recovery; configuration alone cannot prove or enforce residency/lifecycle.
architecture_decisions.decision: Register data assets/flows/processors/profiles and require policy enforcement before data operations, transfers, lifecycle actions and recovery reactivation.

alternatives.name: Storage region flag only
alternatives.summary: Select database location without flow/processor/lifecycle enforcement.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Cannot cover copies, egress, providers, backups, telemetry or truthful evidence.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Policy-backed inventory makes data governance enforceable and evidence-backed across all paths.
consequences: Supportable profiles and lifecycle terms require qualified decisions.
Unknown data destinations are denied by default.

provenance.rationale: Recovery must preserve governed residency/classification profile.

coverage_summary.method: Initial compliance/residency draft mapping; implementation coverage is not yet applicable.

change_history.summary: Initial Enterprise Compliance and Data Residency Layer draft.
change_history.reason: Define enforceable data control before legal/contractual/profile decisions or production data flows.
